To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a distributed data warehouse can be implemented in a geographically distributed corporate structure with the following characteristics: (1) a distributed architecture that supports data localization, (2) a data model that provides a relational model for the fact relation, and (3) a methodology for distributed design of a data warehouse that includes a horizontal fragmentation algorithm.
the data warehouse environment is a new application area for distributed database technology.
the proposed architecture for a distributed data warehousing environment is based upon a distributed relational data model that supports the fact and dimension tables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a distributed data warehouse and the development of a fragmentation algorithm that will allow the fact relation to be fragmented horizontally.
building a distributed data warehouse that will be able to support data localization and data distribution.
the development of a distributed data warehouse that provides an integrated view of data from multiple sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model for a distributed database warehouse is a practical solution to the problem of data distribution in the data warehouse environment.
the proposed distributed data warehouse design methodology is an efficient, effective and economical approach to the design of a distributed data warehouse environment.
the proposed distributed data warehouse model is a good alternative to the centralized one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed and developed a distributed data warehouse that is based on a distributed relational model.
we have developed a distributed data warehouse architecture, a relational data model and a methodology for designing and building distributed data warehouse systems.
we have developed a methodology to design a distributed data warehouse and a fragmentation algorithm for the most important relation in the data warehouse, the fact relation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a distributed data warehouse can be built using the same design methodology used for building a centralized data warehouse, with the exception of the fragmentation algorithm for the “fact” relation.
the data warehouse can be built and maintained at a fraction of the cost of the centralized data warehouse, and the performance can be enhanced through the distribution of the data warehouse.
the design of the data warehouse should take into account its distributed nature and that the design should be based on the data warehouse data model.
